name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt near 5.15% after the BoE's 5 Nov rate rise; yields near multi-decade highs, no weak auction found
state: The 10-year gilt yield edged above 5.15% on 6 Nov after the Bank of England raised rates on 5 Nov for the first time in more than three years, with Governor Bailey saying further tightening may be needed (Trading Economics). Yields remain near their highest since 2007. No weak auction or BoE intervention was found as of 11 Nov, so Watch is kept.
for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage rates and government borrowing costs over the following weeks.

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK bond yields edge up

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
